exely.title: Exely PMS webhook
exely.description:
In Exely: Hotel settings → API connection → your connection → Webhooks: Use webhooks = Yes.
URL: {url}
(Exely accepts only https://; the address must be reachable from the internet. Host: the Internet URL in Settings → System → Network.)
Authentication: API-KEY
Key: {api_key}
Events: check-in, check-out and their cancellations.

Rooms are matched automatically by name or number (Exely Room 01, 01 or 1 → Area Room 01) only when unambiguous. Other numbering (e.g. 101) must be mapped below.

exely_api.title: Exely Connect API
exely_api.description:
Exely webhooks name the booking, not the room. With API access Hotel Sense looks the room up: one request per booking (cached for the stay) plus the room list once a day; never more than 30 requests an hour.

In Exely: Hotel settings → API connection → your connection: client_id and client_secret, with read access to reservations and rooms (PMS API). Property ID: your hotel's ID in Exely (the PropertyId of the webhook events).

Saving checks the access with one room-list request. Leave client_id empty to switch the API off. Now: {status}.
Client secret saved: {secret_saved}.

data_description.exely_client_secret: Leave empty to keep the saved secret.

database.title: History database
database.description:
Hotel Sense keeps its history (Wi-Fi events, who was in which room and when, room states and statuses, Exely events) in its own database, e.g. the MariaDB add-on: host core-mariadb, port 3306. Rows are written in batches every 15 seconds; while the database is down they wait in memory. Rows older than the retention period are deleted every night. Only MACs, SSIDs, rooms and booking numbers are stored - no names or IP addresses.

Saving checks the connection and creates the tables. Leave the user empty to switch the history off.

Now: {status}. Password saved: {password_saved}.

data_description.db_password: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
